parents.instruction: On a scale of 0 (extremely terse, a few short sentences) to 10 (extremely long and verbose, many sentences with elaborate qualification), rate how LONG and VERBOSE the abstract text is -- word count, sentence count, and density of qualifying/elaborating clauses. Score only the extent of length/verbosity; do not judge whether the length is appropriate or whether the paper is good.

parents.criterion: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
parents.instruction: 0-10, extent only. Report how much the abstract advertises artifacts: count how many distinct artifact types are mentioned or promised (for example code, data, models or checkpoints, project or demo pages), whether a concrete link or repository is given, how prominently the advertising is placed, and how often it recurs. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether releasing artifacts is good, whether the artifacts would be useful, complete, usable or reproducible, and you are not judging the research in any way. 0 = no mention of any artifact being available or promised. 3 = one artifact type mentioned in passing, no link. 5 = one or two artifact types clearly promised. 8 = several artifact types promised, or one promised together with a concrete link. 10 = multiple artifact types plus a concrete link or repository, advertised prominently and referred to more than once.
parents.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Artifact-release signaling

parents.criterion: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements
parents.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of explicit release and availability announcements in the abstract: a code URL, a GitHub or project-page or website link, phrases such as 'code is available', 'our data and code will be available', 'code has been released', or the naming of released checkpoints, benchmarks, annotations or datasets as deliverables. 0 = no availability statement of any kind; 3 = a bare promise of future release with no link; 6 = one concrete link or one clearly named released artifact; 10 = several artifacts announced together (for example code plus data plus model weights plus a project page). You must NOT assess whether releasing is good practice, whether the link looks credible or maintained, or whether the artifact is valuable; count only how prominently availability is announced.
parents.upstream_parent: the producing group's release practice and its compliance with venue and reproducibility norms (engineering support, legal clearance, institutional habit)
